In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the two genes is not completely dependent on each other, but that the expression of axl is dependent on the expression of shh.
both genes are expressed in the midline of the developing embryo and that they show some mutual regulation.

the genes involved in the formation of the zebrafish notochord and midline mesodermal tissues are expressed in overlapping patterns and that the regulation of these genes is not completely independent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the zebrafish midline defective genes ntl, flh and cyc are not required for establishment of the organizer but are required for proper development of the midbrain and tail bud.

the expression of axl is regulated by both axial patterning and neuroectoderm development and is not dependent on the endoderm, while shh is regulated by axial patterning and endodermal development, and is independent of neuroectoderm patterning.
the expression domains of both axl (HNF-3 beta) and shh are dynamic and complex, and that the expression of both genes in zebrafish is regulated independently and interdependently.
The main takeaway from our work is that

axl and shhh expression is not restricted to the midline of the embryo and that the midline defects observed in ntl and fl mutants are likely to be due to their effect on the neuroectodermal midline rather than to a direct effect on the expression of axl or shh.
the expression of both genes is not dependent upon the midline mesoderms and that they can be expressed in the absence of the midline.

the expression patterns of the two genes are not simply a result of the presence of a midline but rather reflect the complex interactions of multiple factors that control the development of the vertebrate body axis.
